about.seoDescription: Get to know Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional, a New York community organization rooted in Ecuadorian and Latin American identity, solidarity, and belonging.
about.heroTitle: United by our roots. Driven by our community.
about.heroDescription: At Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional, we work to support, guide, and strengthen Ecuadorian and Latin American communities in New York while sustaining the cultural and human bonds that bring us together.
about.teamPhotoAlt: AEINY community members gathered together around a table.
about.teamPhotoCaption: A community connected by shared roots and care
about.identityTitle: Our roots unite us. Our community moves us forward.
about.identityCopy1: Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional (AEI) is a community organization based in New York, committed to the well-being and development of Ecuadorian and Latin American communities.
about.identityCopy2: Through educational programs, community guidance, cultural activities, and institutional collaboration, we seek to create opportunities and strengthen ties between migrants, their families, and their communities of origin.
about.identityCopy3: Our work connects the needs of people building a life in the United States with recognition of their roots, identity, and contributions to society.
about.storyPhotoAlt: AEINY volunteers and community members gathered with donated food and supplies.
about.missionHeading: A shared purpose, a vision for the future.
about.missionPhotoAlt: AEINY volunteers sharing essential supplies with community members.
about.missionCopy: To support and strengthen Ecuadorian and Latin American communities through access to information, education, guidance, and development opportunities, while encouraging community participation, dignity, and solidarity.
about.visionCopy: An informed, connected, and empowered migrant community with opportunities to thrive and maintain strong ties to its cultural identity and roots.
about.valuesTitle: The values that bring us together
about.rootsPhotoAlt: Community members celebrating Ecuadorian and Latin American heritage at a cultural parade.
about.rootsPhotoCaption: A shared celebration of Ecuadorian and Latin American identity.
about.communityPhotoAlt: AEINY community members sharing a meal and time together.

value.solidarityCopy: We believe in mutual support and in the strength of a community that moves forward together.
value.identityCopy: We value our roots and foster connection across generations and cultures.
value.educationCopy: We see knowledge and learning as tools for opening new opportunities.
value.commitmentCopy: We work to strengthen participation, collaboration, and collective well-being.

about.communityCopy: AEI is built through relationships: neighbors supporting one another, families staying connected, and people finding a sense of belonging across cultures and borders.
about.connectionCopy1: Migration brings change, but it does not erase the stories, language, and traditions that shape who we are.
about.connectionCopy2: We honor the ties between people, families, and places of origin, and the many ways our community carries its identity forward.
about.belongingCopy: We believe everyone deserves to be welcomed with dignity and to have their experiences and contributions recognized. That belief shapes how we listen, build relationships, and move forward together.
about.finalTitle: When a community comes together, opportunities grow.
about.finalDescription: Join a community grounded in solidarity, shared identity, and care for one another.

ourWork.seoTitle: Our Work | Community Support & Education | AEINY
ourWork.seoDescription: Explore how AEINY supports immigrant communities through human rights, education, cultural heritage and community wellbeing.
ourWork.heroDescription: AEINY brings together community support, education, cultural heritage and initiatives for wellbeing to help immigrant communities navigate challenges and build opportunities.
ourWork.heroPhotoAlt: Community members gather together at an AEINY event.
ourWork.approachCopy: For immigrant communities, access to reliable information, opportunities to learn and a sense of belonging can make a meaningful difference. AEINY connects these needs through community-based work shaped by lived experience and cultural identity.

support.title: Migrant Support & Human Rights
support.lead: Access to information is essential for protecting rights and making informed decisions.
support.copy: AEINY's community work addresses issues relevant to immigrants, workers and families, including migration, labor rights, discrimination and participation in civic life. The organization supports awareness, community connections and access to information.
support.photoAlt: Community members receive donated supplies through an AEINY community support effort.

highlights.discrimination: Awareness of discrimination and human rights

education.title: Education & Training
education.lead: Practical learning can open doors to safer work and greater independence.
education.copy: Education and professional preparation are important parts of AEINY's community work. Through Centro Comunitario Andino, the organization has offered learning opportunities, including construction-industry safety training and information relevant to workers and families.
education.photoAlt: Participants attend a workforce training class.

culture.title: Culture & Heritage
culture.lead: Cultural identity is a living connection between people, places and generations.
culture.copy: AEINY has supported public cultural initiatives that celebrate Ecuadorian and Andean traditions. Through community gatherings, artistic expression and cultural exchange, the organization creates opportunities to preserve heritage and strengthen belonging.
culture.photoAlt: Community members take part in an Ecuadorian cultural parade.

wellbeing.title: Community Health & Wellbeing
wellbeing.lead: Healthy communities grow through connection, participation and care.
wellbeing.copy: AEINY's community history includes initiatives that encourage physical activity, collective participation and awareness of wellbeing. Activities such as the historical El Chasqui run-walk demonstrate how cultural identity and healthy living can come together.
wellbeing.photoAlt: Community members take part in a group activity promoting connection and wellbeing.

ourWork.centerLead: Learning that connects people with opportunity.
ourWork.centerCopy: Centro Comunitario Andino is an educational and community space associated with AEINY. Its documented work includes construction training, occupational safety education, cultural identity, and information on migration, labor issues and human rights.
ourWork.centerPhotoAlt: Community members attend a safety training session in a classroom.

listen.title: Listen
listen.copy: We recognize the needs and experiences of immigrant communities.

connect.title: Connect
connect.copy: We bring people, knowledge and community opportunities together.

strengthen.title: Strengthen
strengthen.copy: We support learning, cultural continuity and participation.

ourWork.finalTitle: Looking for information or a way to contribute?
ourWork.finalCopy: Connect with AEINY to learn more about its community initiatives and opportunities for participation.

projects.heroDescription: Explore initiatives that connect migration, collective memory, cultural identity and the future of communities in New York and Ecuador.
projects.introCopy: AEINY's projects recognize the contributions of migrants, preserve collective memory and create ways for communities in New York and Ecuador to stay connected.
projects.parqueLead: A place of recognition for the courage, work and contributions of Ecuadorian migrants.
projects.parqueCopy1: Parque del Migrante is an initiative presented by AEINY to honor the experience and contributions of Ecuadorian migrants. The project envisions a public space in Cuenca dedicated to memory, cultural identity and connection between communities at home and abroad.
projects.parqueCopy2: A publicly presented design includes concepts for an entrance, museum, acoustic performance space, fountain and supporting facilities.

projects.encuentroLead: Connecting the Cuencano community through dialogue, identity and shared opportunities.
projects.encuentroCopy1: The first Cuencano gathering in New York brought together members of the community around concerns affecting migrants, opportunities for entrepreneurship and employment, and ideas for future initiatives in Cuenca.
projects.encuentroCopy2: Its published objectives included discussing the community's situation, exploring future projects in Cuenca and organizing representation in the Ecuadorian cultural parade.

projects.impactCopy: Whether recognizing the contributions of migrants or creating spaces for community dialogue, AEINY's initiatives seek to preserve shared histories, strengthen connections and support collective participation.

festival2026.seoTitle: 1st International Andean Film Festival New York 2026 | Kuri Chasqui Awards | AEINY
festival2026.seoDescription: Discover the 1st International Andean Film Festival New York 2026 and the Kuri Chasqui Awards, celebrating Andean cinema, culture, identity and audiovisual storytelling.
festival2026.title: 1st International Andean Film Festival New York 2026
festival2026.heroIntro: A celebration of Andean cinema, cultural identity, migration, memory and the voices connecting the Andes with the world.
festival2026.heroImageAlt: Community members taking part in a cultural parade.
festival2026.heroImageCaption: Culture and community, at the heart of AEINY.
festival2026.aboutAside: An AEINY cultural initiative connecting filmmakers, artists and communities across countries.
festival2026.aboutCopy: Founded and directed by Walther Sinche and Amaruk Kayshapanta, the International Andean Film Festival is a cultural platform dedicated to audiovisual works related to Andean cultures, identity, migration, human rights, memory and contemporary social realities.
festival2026.awardsCopy: “Kuri Chasqui” is a Kichwa / Quechua expression translated by the organizers as “The Golden Messenger.” The awards recognize outstanding audiovisual professionals and works connected with Andean cinema and culture.
festival2026.awardsContext: The name draws on Andean cosmovision, ancestral philosophy and the cultures of Tawantinsuyu and South America. The awards are planned as annual international Andean film awards beginning in 2026.
festival2026.awardRecognition: A symbol of transmitting knowledge, culture, memory and Andean worldview.

kuri2026Page.seoTitle: 1st International Andean Film Festival New York 2026 | Kuri Chasqui Awards | AEINY
kuri2026Page.seoDescription: Discover the 1st International Andean Film Festival New York 2026 and the Kuri Chasqui Awards, celebrating Andean cinema, identity, memory and culture.
kuri2026Page.heroTitle: 1st International Andean Film Festival New York 2026
kuri2026Page.heroSupporting: Andean cinema arrives in the heart of New York.
kuri2026Page.posterAlt: Official poster for the 1st International Andean Film Festival New York 2026.
kuri2026Page.aboutTitle: Stories, memory and identity of the Andes—on screen in New York.
kuri2026Page.aboutCopy: Kuri Chasqui is a cultural platform created to bring the stories, memory and identity of the Andes to New York through cinema. Born from the intersection of social activism, Indigenous identity and artistic expression, the festival creates a space where the Andean diaspora can reconnect with its roots while sharing its stories with a wider audience.
kuri2026Page.whyTitle: Why Andean cinema matters in New York
kuri2026Page.whyCopyOne: For migrant communities from Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia and Colombia in New York, Andean cinema can be a direct connection to home. It gives visibility to Indigenous and rural cultures, and helps preserve stories, memory and language across generations.
kuri2026Page.whyCopyTwo: Many Andean productions incorporate Indigenous languages such as Kichwa and Aimara. Hearing these languages in a New York cinema gives them public space and can help younger generations stay connected to their heritage.
kuri2026Page.rootsDescription: Connecting diaspora communities with their cultural heritage.
kuri2026Page.visibilityDescription: Giving space to Indigenous, rural and Andean identities.
kuri2026Page.memoryDescription: Using cinema as a living archive of migration, history and language.
kuri2026Page.connectionDescription: Bringing filmmakers, communities and audiences together in New York.
kuri2026Page.editionTitle: Andean stories, shared in New York.
kuri2026Page.editionCopy: The planned programming brings together community cinema, documentaries about migrant memory and award-winning feature films from the region.
kuri2026Page.programTitle: Eight days of cinema and community.
kuri2026Page.awardCopy: The Kuri Chasqui statuette is the official distinction awarded to festival winners. Designed specifically for this event, it brings together pre-Columbian heritage and the contemporary artistic experience of the Andean diaspora.
kuri2026Page.awardImagePlaceholder: Official statuette image to be added when available.
